bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Intense low-cost steel imports; unethical competition in core wire; biotech commercialization delay; welding margin recovery slower than expected
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, strategic, disciplined; framing challenges as temporary, emphasizing transformation, brand-building, and financial prudence
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Biotech is not a grant-dependent initiative — it's a pure B2B business model targeting distilleries with ₹1/litre product; BIS/RDSO approval for welding is a rare, high-barrier credential in railway infrastructure
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet has been deleveraged: Debt-to-Equity fell from 0.29 in FY22 to near-zero (0.00-0.05) in FY23-FY26, while Equity grew from ₹77.94 Cr (FY22) to ₹124.27 Cr (FY26).
- Dividend per share has stepped down as equity/capacity expanded — ₹2 (FY22), ₹2 (FY23), ₹1 (FY24), ₹0.5 (FY25), ₹0 (FY26, provisional).
- ROCE has declined sharply from 45.70% (FY22) to 4.03% (FY26, provisional estimate) as the equity base grew faster than returns.
- Promoter-dominated shareholding register with minimal FII ownership (0.14%).
- Management commentary frames capital allocation philosophy explicitly: 'strengthening our core, cash-generating businesses while pursuing new opportunities with capital discipline and a focus on long-term value creation.'
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Expertise in precision metallurgy and a role in advancing and fine-tuning steel manufacturing processes
- Preferred supplier status with some of India's largest steel players, built on quality and manufacturing expertise
- Locational advantage: headquartered in Bhilai, Chhattisgarh, close to a major steel production hub, enabling efficient connectivity and robust industry partnerships
- ISO 9001 certified facilities with rigorous testing and inspection ensuring consistent product quality
- Certification moat in welding consumables - BIS, CE and Boiler & Pressure Vessel certifications plus the April 2025 RDSO approval from Indian Railways, which opens doors with major construction and engineering companies
- Dealer-led distribution model spanning more than 10 dealers across more than five states, with rising repeat orders as the Company's brands gain traction
- Virtually debt-free balance sheet giving flexibility to fund growth from a position of strength
- Diversified three-pillar portfolio - core metallurgical consumables, welding consumables and biotechnology
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Commodity price volatility — Volatility in commodity prices, particularly ferro alloys and aluminium, driven by global and domestic supply-demand dynamics, can materially affect input costs and margins. Mitigated by continuous tracking of commodity trends, agile pricing, product-mix diversification and evaluation of hedging instruments.
- Regulatory and trade-policy risk — Shifts in trade policy, including the withdrawal of protective measures such as safeguard duties or quality control orders, could affect margins and the competitive position of domestic manufacturing. Mitigated by close policy tracking, widening the market footprint to reduce dependence on any single geography or policy regime, and working with industry bodies.
- Import-driven competition and pricing distortions in specialised downstream products — Global steel prices and low-cost imports weighed on domestic manufacturers and allied industries over the previous two years; even after the 12% safeguard duty on flat steel imports and stricter quality norms, persistent unfair competition and pricing distortions continue to affect parts of the value chain, particularly specialised downstream products, demanding continued discipline from ancillary suppliers such as the Company.
- Segment overcapacity - Aluminium Flipping Coils — Significant overcapacity in the domestic market kept the segment subdued through the year; the Company consciously refrained from unviable price competition to protect profitability, which constrains volumes until market conditions stabilise and commercial viability improves.
- Project management / execution risk in newer businesses — Delays or inefficiencies in executing capital projects, including capacity expansions in newer businesses, may cause cost escalation and defer planned growth. Mitigated by structured planning frameworks, detailed feasibility studies and risk analyses before committing capital, and cross-functional issue resolution.
- Supply chain concentration and disruption — Disruptions from environmental events, geopolitical tensions or concentration among suppliers can affect operational continuity and cost efficiency. Mitigated by alternative sourcing channels, a diversified supplier base, improved supply chain visibility and contingency plans.
- Credit risk on receivables — Defaults by customers on payment obligations expose the Company to credit risk; significant defaults can strain cash flows and profitability. Mitigated by thorough credit assessment, keeping the customer portfolio broad to avoid overdependence on a few accounts, defined credit terms and close receivables monitoring.
- Safety risk in manufacturing operations — Manufacturing operations demand the highest safety standards; any lapse in safety protocols can disrupt operations, invite legal consequences and damage the Company's reputation. Mitigated by rigorous protocols with continuous training, periodic safety audits and detailed risk assessments across facilities, and a safety-first culture at every level.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- India's leading manufacturer & exporter of Cored Wires & Aluminium Flipping Coils, and a preferred supplier to some of India's largest steel units; HQ in Bhilai, Chhattisgarh, close to a critical steel hub.
- Part of the ₹650+ Cr Desraj Bansal (DB) Group, which also houses Sarthak Energy Pvt Ltd (solar) and Bansal Brothers (ferroalloys, 11,000 TPA capacity) under one group umbrella in Bhilai.
- 85% repeat business and 10+-year relationships across steel plants, fabrication units and foundries; top-5 clients contribute 40% of sales; 150+ customers served to date with 25+ new clients onboarded in FY26.
- In ferro titanium, management cites 'technical expertise and relatively limited competition' as a particular area of strength within the cored wire portfolio.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Regulatory] UAE's June 2026 ban on aluminium scrap exports, plus similar restrictions in an increasing number of countries, is tightening global scrap availability and raising scrap prices — a direct headwind to the Aluminium Flipping Coils segment, which the company says it is 'monitoring closely.'
- [Sector context] India's BioEconomy crossed an estimated $92 billion in 2022, with a policy/industry target of $150 Bn by 2025 and $300 Bn by 2030 (~17% CAGR) — cited as the backdrop for the company's biotech optionality, not a company-specific figure.
- [Group entity] Bansal Brothers (DB Group) has a separate 11,000 TPA ferroalloys capacity, outside SMLT's own listed entity.
- [Corporate history] Incorporated 1995 (originally an industrial gases unit, sold in 2021); commenced Aluminium Flipping Coils 2002; first in-house Cored Wire mill 2008; started Cored Wire feeder machines 2012; IPO & BSE SME listing 2017; entered Flux Cored Wire business 2018; commenced backward integration into aluminium wire rods for flipping coils 2023; ventured into biotech (bioethanol/biogas, Nagpur) 2024; migrated to/listed on the BSE Main Board since Nov 25, 2021 per the share-price slide.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Sarthak Metals manufactures and exports metallurgical consumables - principally Cored Wires and Aluminium Flipping Coils - used to advance and fine-tune steel manufacturing processes, and is the preferred supplier to some of India's largest steel players. Headquartered in Bhilai, Chhattisgarh, it leverages proximity to a major steel production hub and operates ISO 9001 certified facilities with rigorous testing and inspection. Welding consumables, led by Flux Cored Wires, have emerged as the new growth engine, with seven grades across carbon steel, stainless steel and hardfacing at a capacity of 3,600 TPA sold through a dealer-led model, while a pilot Solid State Fermentation R&D facility at Nagpur marks a measured entry into enzyme technologies for the ethanol ecosystem.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Evolve from a steel consumables supplier into a diversified company standing on three pillars: a core business of cored wires and aluminium flipping coils, welding consumables as a quality-driven growth engine, and biotechnology as a future frontier - a portfolio deliberately structured so the core tracks steel-led cycles while newer ventures follow infrastructure-driven trends, giving a measure of protection against cyclicality
- Scale the welding consumables (Flux Cored Wires) division from venture to core growth driver, building the brand and deepening the dealer network that currently contributes around 90% of divisional sales
- Deepen value in existing verticals by broadening the cored wire range to include variants tailored for foundries and emerging industrial applications
- Introduce innovative new variants within the Flux Cored Wire segment to drive further market penetration and customer acquisition
- Find new applications for Flux Cored Wires across construction, shipbuilding, railways and fabrication to diversify revenue sources and enhance product relevance in allied sectors
- Scale global reach by entering new markets and strengthening engagement in existing export markets, diversifying revenue streams and enhancing overall realisations
- Counter sub-par quality products and inadequate service standards through knowledge-driven marketing, reliable technical support and consistent product performance, while deepening engagement with the key customers who form the backbone of the business
- Stay away from unviable price competition in aluminium flipping coils to protect profitability, and normalise operations once market conditions stabilise and commercial viability improves
- Pursue biotechnology patiently and with capital discipline - integrating Solid State Fermentation technology with leading ethanol distilleries to improve fermentation efficiency, lower operating costs and support cleaner ethanol production
- Embed sustainability into core operations - captive solar power, recycled aluminium scrap in coil production, and leaner inventory and working capital
- Fund new growth areas from a virtually debt-free balance sheet with healthy reserves, without straining resources
- Safety-first culture embedded at every level of the organisation, reinforced through continuous training programmes and supported by periodic safety audits and detailed risk assessments across facilities
- Human capital: team strength of 149 individuals as of March 31, 2026, structured training and development initiatives building technical and professional capability, an inclusive and collaborative workplace, and industrial relations that remained harmonious through the year
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report describes no rupee-denominated capex programme; expansion is disclosed as capacity, footprint and approvals. In welding consumables the Company now manufactures seven grades across three categories - carbon steel, stainless steel and hardfacing - at a capacity of 3,600 TPA, with BIS, CE and Boiler & Pressure Vessel certifications and vendor approvals from leading institutions; the RDSO approval received from Indian Railways in April 2025 opens doors with major construction and engineering companies, and the division completed its first full year of operations having sold more than 1,400 tonnes at average monthly volumes exceeding 115 tonnes. Distribution capacity has been built out through a dealer-led model spanning more than 10 dealers across more than five states. The newest expansion frontier is biotechnology: a pilot Solid State Fermentation (SSF) R&D facility at Nagpur became operational during the year, with the first fermentation batch commencing in May 2025, focused on enzyme technologies for the ethanol ecosystem; discussions are underway with leading ethanol distilleries and investment has been kept deliberate and capital-disciplined while the segment's long-term potential takes shape. A 400 KW solar power plant at the facility supplies captive power and has reduced electricity costs by nearly 50%. Management flags project management risk explicitly, noting that delays or inefficiencies in executing capital projects, including capacity expansions in newer businesses, may cause cost escalation and defer planned growth, and states that detailed feasibility studies and risk analyses are completed before committing capital. The Board reports no material changes or commitments affecting the financial position between the year end and the date of the report.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India remains one of the most attractive long-term steel markets globally, supported by sustained investment in infrastructure, railways, housing, manufacturing and government-led capital expenditure, with the country targeting 300 million tonnes of steel capacity by 2030
- Policy support strengthened: the 12% safeguard duty introduced in 2025 and stricter quality norms have raised the industry's quality benchmark and eased import pressure
- Offsetting headwind: global steel prices near five-year lows keep imports competitive, and persistent unfair competition and pricing distortions continue to affect parts of the value chain, particularly specialised downstream products
- Core cored wire business regaining ground - volumes grew 14% in FY26 with fourth-quarter volumes rising 32% year-on-year
- Aluminium flipping coils remained subdued amid significant overcapacity and difficult domestic market conditions; the fourth quarter brought an encouraging recovery in volumes and management is prepared to normalise operations as commercial viability improves
- Welding consumables demand from the fabrication and construction sectors remains robust, with the RDSO approval and BIS certification opening doors with major construction and engineering companies and repeat orders rising as the brands gain traction
- The government's fuel blending programme has created a bio-consumables opportunity management estimates at over Rs 1,000 Crore, though significant ethanol industry capacity additions in recent years argue for a measured approach
- Sustainability is becoming a commercial driver - the EU's carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM) is an imminent reality and the Indian steel industry must move towards going green; captive solar has reduced electricity costs by nearly 50% and over 75% of aluminium production uses recycled scrap
- No formal order book is disclosed; management notes that repeat orders in the welding consumables division are rising as the Company's brands gain traction, with more than 10 dealers across more than five states contributing around 90% of the division's sales currently
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Sarthak Metals is transforming from a cyclical steel inputs player into a diversified industrial group with high-margin welding and biotech divisions, offsetting core business decline driven by import pressure; the biotech entry into ethanol distilleries is the most significant strategic shift, creating a new growth pillar with high-margin potential.
